request.feedback: REJECT R1-INTAKE-001: launcher restrictions now intercept unrelated legacy Telegram formats before explicit namespace selection. telegram_launcher.py:276 unconditionally rejects every channel_post when enabled; telegram_launcher_intake.py:176-193 requires launcher prepare permission (and rejects captions) for every document before checking its kind. This breaks the approved architecture requirement that pre-existing JSON formats retain original dispatch and the no-flag legacy behavior. Reproduced locally: a non-launcher legacy channel_post returns 400 UNSUPPORTED_UPDATE; a legacy .json upload by a prompt-only but otherwise legacy-allowed user returns 403 ACCESS_DENIED before the legacy handler. Stage2 returned None for both. Restrict these rules to explicitly selected launcher intake, preserving old text/document/channel routes; use an unambiguous launcher document selector/route if needed to maintain authorization before download. Do not solve by weakening launcher authorization or allowing unauthenticated new-envelope downloads. Add enabled-mode integration tests for legacy text, document (including old caption semantics), and channel posts plus unauthorized launcher no-download tests, and align intake documentation. Independent combined suites passed 108 tests; full concurrent duplicate-intake probe produced one operation and one published intent without activation. Shared reservation, immutable publication, source pinning and PREPARATION_REQUIRED boundary otherwise match stage scope.
